---
title: "Building and running"
---

## Image

The `Containerfile` downloads the official graywolf release tarball for the
target architecture (`amd64` or `arm64`, e.g. Raspberry Pi 5), verifies its
SHA-256 against the release `checksums.txt`, and installs it on
`debian:trixie-slim`. The version is the `GRAYWOLF_VERSION` build arg
(default `0.14.14`, also set in `compose.yaml`).

State (config DB, packet history, map tiles) lives in `./graywolf-data/`
(bind-mounted at `/data` with `:U` so podman chowns it to the container user).
It is git-ignored; back it up to keep your station config. The web UI listens on port 8080.

## Running without a radio (APRS-IS only)

```bash
podman compose up -d --build
```

Then browse to <http://localhost:8080>.

## Running with a Digirig

```bash
podman compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.digirig.yaml up -d --build
```

`compose.digirig.yaml` passes `/dev/snd` (Digirig audio) and the CP210x serial
port (PTT via RTS/DTR) into the container. Plug the Digirig in first; a missing
device stops the container from starting.

- Serial port other than `/dev/ttyUSB0`:
  `DIGIRIG_SERIAL=/dev/ttyUSB1 podman compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.digirig.yaml up -d`
- Rootless podman needs your host user in the `audio` and `dialout` groups
  (`sudo usermod -aG audio,dialout $USER`, then log in again). The overlay uses
  `group_add: keep-groups` so the container user inherits them.
- In the graywolf UI, select the Digirig sound device and serial PTT (RTS).

## Building for another architecture

```bash
podman build --platform linux/arm64 -t graywolf:arm64 .
```

This needs QEMU binfmt emulation on the build host; on the Pi itself a plain
`podman compose build` builds natively.
